4.text: of meat usually consumed by the Reindeer and by the Maritime Chukchee is

6.text: Every adult member of a Chukchee family, and each child after he is

7.text: about five years old, has his own eating-knife. Often these knives are simply

8.text: small bits of iron, rudely set in a handle, and unfit for many uses.

23.text: The Chukchee usually carry their knives in their belts, while the Lamut

24.text: and the Russo-Yukaghir have the scabbard fastened to the hip by means of

25.text: a loop of leather, and a toggle formed simply by a knot of the string.

27.text: in northern Asia. Among the more ancient stone blades there are some which

35.text: Knife-sharpeners are made of slender pieces

36.text: of sandstone of fine grain. At Indian Point I found such a sharpener, made

37.text: of jade, and pierced through at one end for convenience in fastening it to the

38.text: belt. It was said to have come from King’s Island. In the Koryak villages

39.text: of western Kamchatka, knife-sharpeners are made of pieces of petrified wood,

40.text: which is frequently found on the seashore near the mouths of rivers.

41.text: Large whetstones for sharpening tools are made of square blocks of

42.text: smooth-grained sandstone, which is found in various places about the country.

43.text: A few revolving grindstones have been bought from the Russians and Americans.
